study type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
exposure: Mode of delivery in the first pregnancy
Duration of labor in the first pregnancy
caesarean section (CS) in the first or second stage of labour
outcome: Gestational length in the second pregnancy
Mode of delivery in the second pregnancy
Neonatal unit admission in the second pregnancy
Preterm birth rate in the second pregnancy
cohort: 30,840 women with spontaneous onset of labor in their first pregnancy and a subsequent birth reported in the same database
finding: Compared with vaginal birth, an emergency cesarean section in the first pregnancy is associated with a shorter gestational length, increased rate of repeat cesarean section, and increased risk of neonatal unit admission in the next pregnancy.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean section in the first pregnancy is associated with shorter gestational length, increased rate of repeat cesarean section, and increased risk of neonatal unit admission in the subsequent pregnancy.
